Method of Attack: Gaining access to bank employee's email account via malware or reused passwords from leaked datasets
Sending spear-phishing emails with CHM file attachments containing JavaScript to download and install first-stage malware dropper
Dropper collects data and sends to command and control (C&C) servers
If PC deemed valuable, second-stage Silence trojan is sent which takes repeated screenshots to create a pseudo-video stream of user activity
Use of legitimate Windows administration tools for post-exploitation to evade detection
Impacted Systems: Banks in Russia, Armenia, and Malaysia
Attack Vector: Compromised bank employee email accounts via spear-phishing emails with malicious CHM attachments
Indicators of Compromise: CHM file attachments in spear-phishing emails
Repeated desktop screenshots uploaded to C&C servers
